subtopic: Schedule II and III quantity limits
stem: During a controlled-substance review, a buprenorphine prescription for opioid use disorder requests a 90-day single fill. Which Massachusetts quantity pathway is relevant?

choices.text: Apply a 30-day ceiling because no Schedule III opioid can qualify for 90 days.
Use 90 days merely because every Schedule III drug qualifies.
Apply the initial-opiate seven-day limit even though the drug is prescribed for OUD.
The Schedule III opioid-use-disorder treatment pathway may allow up to a 90-day single fill if no other restriction controls.
Convert six authorized refills into one 90-day supply.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'The Schedule III opioid-use-disorder treatment pathway may allow up to a 90-day single fill if no other restriction controls.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Apply a 30-day ceiling because no Schedule III opioid can qualify for 90 days.' would require that the Massachusetts OUD-drug pathway were unavailable. The decisive cue appears in 'During a controlled-substance review, a buprenorphine prescription for opioid use disorder requests a 90-day single fill. Which Massachusetts quantity pathway is relevant?'.

Which Massachusetts quantity pathway is relevant?' states otherwise.

related_facts: buprenorphine (Subutex) is used for treatment of opioid dependence; it is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III.

Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps.
